text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The board of the International Monetary Fund meets in Washington on Friday to approve the final agreement between Egypt and the fund, paving the way for the Paris Club to waive a last tranche of debt, worth $4 billion.
- At its weekly meeting today, the cabinet will discuss giant electricity projects in the provinces to meet the needs of 40 areas and industrial complexes.
- President Hosni Mubarak has dismissed the deputy governor of Cairo and another Cairo official for negligence. They failed to prevent a mansion being demolished in Garden City.
- Mubarak gives interview to Time magazine.
- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi announced that legal measures are being taken to bring back people who have fled the country after committing financial crimes.
- Twenty-one million people, all those with health insurance, will qualify to take advantage of President Mubarak's decision to open military hospitals to the general public.
- Germany gives Egypt 287 million marks in grants and loans.
- The cabinet meeting today will discuss peace in the Middle East and talks with the International Monetary Fund.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Egypt was following closely the Erez negotiations and that the talks between Mubarak and Arafat in Ismailia on Monday night were to study the state of the negotiations.
- Tourism Minister Mamdouh el-Beltagi says Egypt will receive six million tourists a year by the year 2000.
